# Surface — what each package exports, and what anyone outside it reaches

Generated by `fli ws:surface`. **Do not edit.**

`exports.snapshot.md` is what a package SHIPS; this is what is REACHED. Two
questions, both read off the tree: an `exports` entry no file outside the package
imports, and an exported name no file outside the package mentions. A surface
that grows with no caller is cost with no buyer, and this is where it is counted.

**Unreached is a question, not a verdict.** A name is reached when its identifier
appears in any source file outside its package — the loosest honest reading, so a
common word is never called dead and a dead name may pass as reached. Linked
prototypes outside this repo are not scanned here (`fli ws:surface --also <dir>`
asks them, in the terminal), so a name below may be live there. An error class
exported for `instanceof`, a type a consumer would import, a helper a test reaches
by relative path — each is a reason, and the row is where the reason gets asked for.

**Emitted** is a name or an entry no outside file mentions but a string the package
itself writes out does — the mesa compiler emits its runtime's names into compiled
output no source file holds, and sierra's auto-import writes the import of its own
root into every page. Counted apart, never as unreached.

Only crossings are recorded — no importer, no reach — so the file moves when a
surface gains an unreached export or loses its last caller, and not on every import.
